explanation: The brown dots under a fern leaf are clusters of spore cases. As each case dries, a ring of cells snaps it open like a catapult, flinging spores into the air.

claims.text: Ferns reproduce by releasing spores rather than seeds.
Ferns do not produce pollen, nuts or berries.
The brown dots on the undersides of fern leaves are clusters of spore cases.
As fern spore cases dry, a ring of cells flings the spores out like a catapult.

evidence.restatement: Ferns reproduce by releasing spores, not seeds.
Ferns produce no flowers, so no pollen, nuts or berries.
The brown dots under fern fronds are sori, clusters of spore cases (sporangia).
As a sporangium dries, its annulus, a ring of cells, snaps it open like a catapult and flings out the spores.
